channel.title: ROMRx Base Articles
channel.description: Evidence-based range of motion, mobility, and flexibility guides from ROMRx.

item.title: Mobility vs Flexibility: What's the Difference?
item.description: Mobility vs flexibility is not the same as range of motion. Learn the difference, why it changes how you train, and how to test your own active range.

item.title: Normal Range of Motion by Joint (Degrees Chart)
item.description: See a normal range of motion chart for the neck, shoulder, hip, knee, and ankle in degrees, why norms are guides not cutoffs, and how to check your own.

item.title: How to Measure Range of Motion and Track Progress
item.description: Learn how to measure range of motion at home with tape tests, photos, and goniometer apps, then track active and passive range against your own baseline.

item.title: How Long to Hold a Stretch (What Research Says)
item.description: How long to hold a stretch for real flexibility gains: research points to short holds done often, with total weekly time mattering more than any single hold.

item.title: Static vs Dynamic Stretching: Which and When
item.description: Static vs dynamic stretching before a workout: see what research shows about strength, power, and range of motion, and how to structure a smart warm-up.

item.title: Do You Need to Warm Up? What the Evidence Says
item.description: Is a warm up worth the time before training? See what research shows about performance and injury risk, and follow a short, effective dynamic warm up.

item.title: Does Foam Rolling Improve Range of Motion?
item.description: Does foam rolling improve range of motion? Reviews show short-term gains and recovery help. See how it compares with stretching and how to use it well.

item.title: Full vs Partial Range of Motion: What Builds More?
item.description: Full vs partial range of motion for muscle and strength: see what meta-analyses show about long-length training, lengthened partials, and when partials help.

item.title: Hip Mobility for Squats: A How-To Guide
item.description: Improve hip mobility for squats with evidence-informed drills, learn why stance and foot angle matter, and train strength through your new range so it sticks.

item.title: Ankle Dorsiflexion for Squats: Test and Fix It
item.description: Limited ankle dorsiflexion wrecks squat depth. Learn the knee-to-wall test, the numbers that matter, and drills to build usable range you can load.

item.title: Hip Impingement or Tight Hips When You Squat?
item.description: A pinch in the front of the hip at squat depth is not always tightness. Learn what hip impingement is, the signs that suggest it, and when to see a clinician.

item.title: Overhead Shoulder Mobility: Drills That Work
item.description: Struggling to get your arms fully overhead? Learn what limits overhead shoulder mobility, drills that build range, and the signs that mean see a clinician.

item.title: Thoracic Spine Mobility: Best Upper-Back Drills
item.description: A stiff upper back limits overhead reach and rotation. Learn thoracic spine mobility drills for extension and rotation, and how to strengthen your new range.

item.title: Can't Touch Your Toes? Here's Why and What Helps
item.description: Can't touch your toes? It is usually hamstring extensibility plus stretch tolerance, not a fixed limit. Learn what the test measures and how to improve it.

item.title: Stiff Neck and Limited Range: Causes, Red Flags
item.description: A stiff neck with limited turning is common and often posture-related, but some signs need a clinician. Learn the causes, gentle drills, and the red flags.

item.title: Knee Range of Motion: Bend and Straighten Guide
item.description: Learn normal knee range of motion, why a knee may not fully bend or straighten, and the signs like locking or giving way that need a clinician.

item.title: Does Flexibility Decline With Age? What to Do
item.description: Range of motion tends to decline with age, but much stiffness is from inactivity. Learn what flexibility decline with age involves and how to train it back.

item.title: Am I Hypermobile? The Beighton Score Explained
item.description: Learn what joint hypermobility is, how the Beighton score works, how it differs from EDS, and when to see a clinician. This is screening, not diagnosis.

item.title: One Side More Flexible? Why, and What to Do
item.description: One side more flexible than the other is common and usually normal. Learn why the asymmetry happens, when it matters, and how to train the tighter side.

item.title: Hip Mobility for BJJ: Build a Better Guard
item.description: Better guard starts at the hips. Learn evidence-informed hip mobility for BJJ, end-range strength drills for grappling, and how to test and track your range.
